page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-32GB is a compute-oriented virtual server instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7542 processor on KVM virtualization. The configuration provisions 16 shared x86_64 vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz across 16 physical cores with a single thread per core, accompanied by 32 GB of system memory. This sets a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes 16 MB of L3 cache, standard instruction sets including AVX, AES, and SHA extensions, but does not bundle local storage, dedicated hardware accelerators, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread execution in burst-friendly tests, scoring 2,197 in Geekbench single-core and reaching top-tier performance in Geekbench text processing at 2,941 points. Multi-core compute performance remains in the average tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 28,467.64 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 149.22 GB/sec. However, sustained workloads under stress-ng yield lower single-core efficiency at 785.99 points. Uncached memory throughput represents a distinct operational tradeoff, measuring 24.65 GB/sec for read operations and 19.33 GB/sec for write operations.

The shared-core provisioning model delivers favorable compute density for horizontally scalable applications without demanding dedicated host commitments. Given the 1:2 resource allocation and lack of bundled local NVMe storage, UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-32GB is well aligned with stateless microservices, Clang-based CI/CD compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters handling up to 23.31 million operations per second, and distributed web serving tiers backed by remote storage volumes.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-32GB is a compute-focused cloud server built on AMD EPYC 7542 processors running KVM virtualization. It supplies 16 shared x86_64 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz alongside 32 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory distribution of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no bundled local disks or GPUs, requiring networked storage volumes for persistent data. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits solid instruction throughput with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,197 and strong text processing, while sustained heavy CPU stress and uncached memory bandwidth show comparatively lower throughput. Delivering balanced multi-core scaling at an accessible resource tier, it fits stateless application serving, CI/CD compilation tasks, distributed caching, and microservice infrastructure.
